document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Secret] Open-source summary quoting a letter ostensibly signed by Jalaluddin Haqqani, whose network is 'very closely aligned with Al Qaeda', denouncing Mullah Omar. The letter is suspected to be a fake. ISAF analyst commentary calls separating the Taliban from al-Qaeda a farfetched concept, since the same low-level fighters are used by both and al-Qaeda plays a coordinating and strategic role.

events.description: Mullah Omar issued a statement seeking legitimate relations with all countries and expressing solidarity with Iran; Al Qaeda websites denounced the 'nationalist trend'.
Forged letter signed in name of Jalaluddin Haqqani denounced Mullah Omar; suspected psychological operation.
Meetings in Mecca under the Saudi king between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures, backed by the US.
Hekmatyar sent letter to Karzai; similar message in October.
Coalition raid on a home in Kundi village north of Khost city; two men and a woman killed, six detained; target allegedly Al-Qa'idah-affiliated.
Kabul police shut down ERD Security Company and collected its weapons.
Hekmatyar sent a letter to Karzai in spring, with a similar message sent in October.
Hekmatyar sent a similar message to Karzai in October.
Kabul police shut down ERD Security Company and seized its weapons (Kalashnikovs, 18 PK machine-guns, six pistols).
Foreign forces raided a home in Kundi village, killing two men and a woman, wounding another woman, and detaining people; reported targeting an Al-Qa'idah affiliate.
Mullah Omar issued a statement seeking legitimate relations with all countries and expressing solidarity with Iran; Al Qaeda websites then criticized the Taliban's nationalist orientation.
First set of talks between Afghan officials and former Taliban figures held in Mecca under Saudi king's auspices, backed by the US.
Hekmatyar sent a letter to Karzai in spring saying he is old and implying foreign troops should leave urban centers.
Hekmatyar sent a similar message to Karzai.
A letter bearing Jalaluddin Haqqani's signature denouncing Mullah Omar appeared, suspected to be a psychological operation.

Foreign forces raided a home in Kundi village. Two men and a woman were killed, another woman was wounded, and six people were reportedly detained (locals said three). The operation targeted an Al Qaeda-affiliated person.
AIP reported the Kundi village operation. Acting governor Sabari complained that foreign forces never inform Afghan officials of operations in advance.

key_claims: US/NATO and Afghan government pursue reconciling 'moderate' insurgents while isolating hard-liners close to Al Qaeda.
Haqqani network is portrayed as independent of Mullah Omar's Taliban and closely aligned with Al Qaeda.
A letter attributed to Jalaluddin Haqqani denouncing Mullah Omar is suspected to be a psychological operation by the Afghan government or allies.
Saudi-hosted Mecca talks involved mostly low-ranking or disaffected former Taliban figures.
The ISAF analyst judges a Taliban–Al Qaida split functionally unlikely since the groups share low-level fighters and are not operationally fused.
Hekmatyar is described as motivated by power and possibly seeking a senior government post.
